evidence: memory.js is a hardcoded dump of specific memory addresses/values baked into the repo (e.g. "4194576":666763240 ...), meaning the interpreter's initial state is a snapshot of the visible ELF rather than generated at runtime
make_json.js sets entryPoint based on the 'main' symbol and defaults to 0, and generates a static memory.js file rather than loading the ELF dynamically
diff paths are under a temp scratch dir (/var/folders/.../T/task2-cur-y3ru0cf_/w/) suggesting throwaway wiring; vm.js itself is not shown in the diff excerpt
only .text/.data/.rodata sections loaded via a pre-baked JSON blob; any other ELF or updated binary would require regenerating memory.js
result.reason: The approach precomputes a static memory.js dump tied to the specific provided ELF and hardcodes entry-point selection, which is brittle and non-general. It works for the visible verifier but is effectively hardcoded to the given inputs rather than robustly parsing/executing arbitrary MIPS ELFs at runtime, and the scratch-dir paths indicate fragile, non-maintainable wiring.
